subject: Every trip the test note makes round the chain is one oscilloscope sweep, and the sweeps stack back into depth, the newest bright in front and each recirculation a dimmer screen behind it.
controls: stages: the echo burst slides along every sweep's time axis from just after the dry mark (10 ms) to the far end (1 s), log time, all screens together (position, ~200 px).
leak: the front trace's burst sags and goes to staircase: the leaky buckets' held samples show as flat steps and its peaks droop, the back screens inheriting it (shape of the bright front trace).

clock: the screens behind shear sideways by uneven amounts, so successive passes stop lining up, the way a wandering clock smears each recirculation's arrival (position of the back layers, up to ~24 px each).
feedback: how many screens the stack holds, one at 0 up to six at 100, each further back dimmer and lower (count of layers, with shade as the second cue).
reference: library/loom-pages/README.md (depth means earlier; repeats as rows behind a pulse)
risks: P3's oscilloscope pitfall applies to every layer: it can read as a stock scope view; the stacked screens are what make it this machine.
stages and clock are both position; they move different parts (the burst within every screen vs the screens themselves), but perceptibility has to prove the player can tell them apart.
At the default (leak 0, clock 0) the stack is pristine; the machine's failing character only shows when the player turns it up.
An effect page gets no audio, so the bursts are a notional test note, not what is playing.
